verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The right-hand equation X_R = 110(C P_*)^{10} is literally the Lean definition: matchingRadius F C = resetRadius Xi C P = Xi * (C*P)^10 with Xi = 110 (NominalProfile.lean:140-141, ShapeTransition.lean:324). The left-hand threshold is encoded differently: instead of the explicit bound C ≥ max{C_0, (R_*/110)^{1/10}/P_*}, Lean states the two consequences the paper wants (C above an arbitrary floor normFloor, and matchingRadius F C above an arbitrary radiusFloor) as a filter statement ∀ᶠ C in atTop (eventually_matching_geometry, line 159). Recovery: the paper's max{·,·} is exactly the explicit witness for that atTop filter, since C ↦ 110(C P_*)^{10} is increasing on C > 0, so 110(C P_*)^{10} ≥ R_* iff C ≥ (R_*/110)^{1/10}/P_*; conversely the atTop statement instantiated at radiusFloor = R_* and normFloor = C_0 gives some C with both properties, which is all the proof uses. Lean carries one extra conjunct in the same filter statement (separation T C P < exp(-8)) that the paper's display does not mention. Noted separately: this block sits in §4.6, Step 1 of the proof of Theorem 4.6, not in the statement of Lemma 4.9 as the task's context field says.
